dominion.text:
* **What Dominion Energy South Carolina likely wants:** To execute its planned 46 kV rebuild from Urquhart to the Aiken PSA tap point for system hardening, leveraging sequential coordination with Georgia Power on shared items like surveys, right-of-way records, and environmental studies.
* **What constrains it:** It faces non-overlapping construction schedules separated by a 1979-day gap—with its own build running from 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31 prior to Georgia Power's 2029-06-01 build start—along with partial location confidence and an undecided scope regarding whether to rebuild the Aiken PSA tap.
* **Concrete ask:** Request that Georgia Power share any available right-of-way records, surveys, and environmental studies relevant to the 22.4-mile vicinity to assist sequential planning and design.

georgia.text:
* **What Georgia Power wants:** To utilize Dominion Energy South Carolina's surveys, right-of-way records, and environmental studies from its earlier rebuild to inform the design of Georgia Power's later rebuild project.
* **What constrains it:** Construction windows do not overlap (a 1979-day time gap with sequential timing), the projects are 22.4 miles apart, and location confidence is partial.
* **One concrete ask:** Share Dominion Energy South Carolina's surveys, right-of-way records, and environmental studies, and clarify if its project scope includes rebuilding the actual Aiken PSA tap.

notes: All six quotes appear on their cited pages. The NNSA July 20, 2026 notice confirms the project name, the Amentum selection, 1 GW plus about 2 GW of gas-to-nuclear generation, and that no lease is final. DC BLOX shows up only in the HOT 98.3 piece. WRHI puts SRS in Aiken, Allendale and Barnwell counties, SC, about 25 miles southeast of Augusta, which is inside the study area. I rejected the "2027" in-service date: it is DOE's April 2025 target for all its sites (the April 3, 2025 page does not name SRS), and WRHI calls it an initial projection that has already slipped (construction late 2025 did not happen; the partner was picked July 2026 instead of end of 2025). The 2026 NNSA and WRDW articles give no construction or operation dates, so in_service should be null. The category is also questionable: this is a data center with its own on-site power plant, not a DESC or Georgia Power transmission project.

The project is real. NNSA (July 20, 2026), Amentum and DC BLOX coverage confirm Amentum was picked to negotiate a phased lease for a 1 GW data center with about 2 GW of gas-then-nuclear generation at SRS in Aiken County, SC, and no lease is signed yet. All six quotes appear verbatim on their pages. The "2027" in-service date should be null: the end-2027 target comes from DOE's April 2025 notice covering many sites and a 2025 WRHI story calling it "initially projected", while NNSA, Amentum, DC BLOX, WRDW and later coverage all say no construction or completion date is set. The timeline check passes only because every date any source mentions (a 2025 start and 2027 completion, both dropped, and nuclear in the early 2030s) falls between 2024 and 2034.

notes: I extracted the SEPA FY24 PDF text (p. 9). Both quotes appear there word for word, the Customer Funding Approval Summary lists "J. Strom Thurmond $2,725,000", and p. 26 says the projects are "owned and operated by the Corps of Engineers". Wikipedia confirms the Columbia County GA / McCormick County SC location, the Savannah River and USACE as operator. Caveats: $2.725M is Thurmond's total approved funding and is only inferred to be its GSU share (the Hartwell/Thurmond numbers don't reconcile exactly to $4.8M). No source says which state the powerhouse is in (the "GA" tag is unverified). There are no work dates, so the 2024-2034 timeline rests only on the Feb 2024 funding and the future-tense "will be completed".

I extracted the text of SEPA's FY2024 annual report (pp. 8-9). Both SEPA quotes appear word for word. The report shows J. Strom Thurmond at $2,725,000 in its Customer Funding Approval Summary but does not break that total down, so reading all of it as the transformer work (cost_usd) is an inference. Wikipedia's infobox confirms the county and river quote and names the USACE as operator. Gridinfo/EIA data also lists USCE-Savannah District as operator but puts the plant at Clarks Hill, SC in McCormick County, so the powerhouse's state tag should likely be SC, not GA. No start or finish dates are published anywhere. The only timing evidence is the February 2024 funding and the report's future tense ("will be completed"), and that is why I place it in 2024-2034. This is generation equipment at a federal dam, not DESC or Georgia Power transmission work.

Wikipedia has the exact quoted sentence, the location (Burke County, near Waynesboro), the owners, and "Unit 4: November 19, 2013" as the construction start. I pulled the text out of the cited MEAG PDF and read the Wikipedia wikitext directly. Both quotes are there. Both sources say Unit 4 entered commercial operation on 2024-04-29, and Wikipedia's infobox and reactor table give its construction start as November 19, 2013. Wikipedia also puts the plant in Burke County near Waynesboro. The Georgia Power release confirms the co-owners (MEAG, Georgia Power, Oglethorpe, Dalton) and that Southern Nuclear operates it. Two caveats: this is a generating unit, not a transmission project, and the cited MEAG PDF sits under a 2026/09 upload path with a 2026-09-14 creation date. The original 2024 release is at /wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Vogtle-Unit-4-COD-Final-4.29.24.pdf, and its text is the same.

method: Project center: midpoint of the two located endpoints, or the one located endpoint.
Distance: straight-line (haversine) miles between centers. An opportunity is a pair under 25 miles apart.
Day gap: days between the two in-service dates (Dominion's planned in-service date, Georgia's need date, and the in-service column of each submitted plan).
Default view: Georgia Power and Georgia Power (Savannah) projects; approximate locations included.
Other utilities: projects found by the research team, each with cited sources, listed when under 25 miles from both sides of an opportunity.
Plans that give only a year or month use the last day of that period; their day gaps are marked 'about'.

report.markdown:
# Coordination opportunities across utility plans

As of 2026-09-26. Every number below comes from the pipeline's code.

## Method

- Project center: midpoint of the two located endpoints, or the one located endpoint.
- Distance: straight-line (haversine) miles between centers. An opportunity is a pair under 25 miles apart.
- Day gap: days between the two in-service dates (Dominion's planned in-service date, Georgia's need date, and the in-service column of each submitted plan).
- Default view: Georgia Power and Georgia Power (Savannah) projects; approximate locations included.
- Other utilities: projects found by the research team, each with cited sources, listed when under 25 miles from both sides of an opportunity.
- Plans that give only a year or month use the last day of that period; their day gaps are marked 'about'.
